targets.name: C54x common core
targets.description: A device-neutral 16-bit C54x CPU target. This is a semantic and interface boundary, not a claim that every C54x device has identical memory, interrupt, timing, or peripheral behavior.
inclusions: CPU instruction and register foundations that are common across the C54x family and supported by pinned TI evidence
Program-word and data-word architectural concepts needed by the common execution contract
Documented reset effects that can be stated without selecting a silicon profile
Instruction sequencing and status effects only when a requirement has an evidence record
exclusions: XPC and any extended program-page or extended-address semantics
Device-specific ROM, RAM, memory maps, wait states, and boot maps
Exact IFR/IMR interrupt sources, vector tables, and device interrupt wiring
Peripherals, PLL and clock setup, electrical behavior, and silicon errata
Machine-cycle or pipeline timing guarantees until timing evidence and tests are added
VC5402-specific behavior, which belongs to the separate profile target

evidence.assertion: The program-control discussion places the current PC value on the program address bus and increments the PC for the next sequential fetch; this establishes the common one-word flow effect without selecting a device memory map.

The program-control register discussion describes the state used to continue sequential program execution; it supports the common sequential PC effect without asserting XPC or an extended-page implementation.

The reset description gives PC=FF80h, IPTR=1FFh, IFR=0, RC=0, ARP=0, ASM=0, AVIS=0, BRAF=0, C16=0, C=1, CLKOFF=0, CMPT=0, CPL=0, DP=0, DROM=0, FRCT=0, HM=0, INTM=1, OVA=0, OVB=0, OVM=0, OVLY=0, SXM=1, TC=1, and XF=1. It discusses XPC only where applicable and that field is excluded from this common target. SP and remaining status bits are not initialized by this reset source, so no value is asserted for them.

ST0 and ST1 are 16-bit status registers. ST0 assigns ARP to bits 15-13, TC to bit 12, C to bit 11, OVA to bit 10, OVB to bit 9, and DP to bits 8-0. ST1 assigns BRAF to bit 15, CPL to bit 14, XF to bit 13, HM to bit 12, INTM to bit 11, reserves bit 10 as read-zero, OVM to bit 9, SXM to bit 8, C16 to bit 7, FRCT to bit 6, CMPT to bit 5, and ASM to bits 4-0; Table 4-1 and Table 4-2 provide the listed reset values.

The status-register description permits ST0 and ST1 to be stored and loaded, permits individual status bits to be set or reset, and describes loading ARP through its documented short-immediate field path. This record does not assert arbitrary data-memory ARP writes, raw status write masks, timing, or reserved-bit semantics.

PMST is a 16-bit processor-mode status register with IPTR in bits 15-7, MP/MC in bit 6, OVLY in bit 5, AVIS in bit 4, DROM in bit 3, CLKOFF in bit 2, SMUL in bit 1, and SST in bit 0. IPTR resets to 1FFh, OVLY, AVIS, DROM, and CLKOFF reset to zero, MP/MC is sampled from the reset pin, and SMUL/SST are not assigned a common reset value on devices where they are unsupported.
The auxiliary-register bank consists of eight 16-bit registers AR0 through AR7 used to generate data-space addresses and as general-purpose registers; this definition does not assign a reset value.
The stack-pointer register SP is a 16-bit register containing the top system-stack address. This register-definition record assigns no reset value.
The common program counter PC is a 16-bit register and Table 6-2 loads FF80h on reset. This record does not establish XPC semantics or any extended program-address behavior.
The single-repeat counter RC is a 16-bit register loaded by repeat instructions. This register-definition record assigns no reset value.

IFR is a memory-mapped interrupt-flag register whose individual interrupt-source meanings vary by device. The common target therefore stores a raw register value without assigning device-specific flag names.

The NOP entry identifies word 0xF495, consumes one program word, has no status-bit effects, and only increments the PC in the common model. Its cycle information is intentionally not adopted as a common-core timing promise.

The direct-addressing discussion defines dma as a 7-bit field; with CPL=0 it concatenates the 9-bit DP field and dma into a 16-bit data-memory word address, while CPL=1 adds positive dma to SP. Direct addressing does not change DP or SP. The source does not specify AR effects or CPL=1 overflow or wrap behavior.
The single-indirect format uses I, MOD, and ARF fields. For CMPT=0, ARF selects the addressed auxiliary register and ARP is not updated by that selection.

The auxiliary-address unit is described as an unsigned 16-bit value and supports premodify ordering where a mode requires it; this record makes no inference about address-domain edges or instruction scheduling.

Table 5-4 defines MOD0 as no modification, MOD1 as decrement after use, MOD2 as increment after use, and MOD3 as increment before use; one-word operands change an auxiliary register by one, and MOD3 is a write-only form.

Table 5-4 defines MOD5 as using the old ARx value for the operand followed by ARx minus AR0, and MOD6 as using the old ARx value followed by ARx plus AR0; this record makes no claim about alias ordering, boundary wrap, or timing.

The indexed-address discussion describes AR0 as an index applied to any other auxiliary register; it does not define selected-AR0 alias ordering, address wrap, circular or bit-reversed behavior, long32 indexed operands, or timing.
The single-indirect description cross-checks postmodify versus premodify order and identifies MOD3 as a write-only form.

Table 5-4 specifies an increment or decrement magnitude of one data word for 16-bit word access and two data words for 32-bit word access. This record intentionally does not restate MOD ordering or the MOD3 write restriction, which remain covered by the existing §5.5.3 and §5.5.3.1 records; it makes no claim about bus selection, cycles, or timing.

The 32-bit data operand is ordered with the first accessed data word as the most-significant word and the second as the least-significant word; an even first address pairs with the next higher word, while an odd first address pairs with the previous lower word. This record makes no claim about bus selection, cycles, or timing.
For CMPT=0, the ARF field selects the auxiliary register, ARP is not updated, and ARP must be zero.
The checked address planner exposes explicit status values and a by-value effect whose rejected-input contract is an all-zero effect. This is a project API contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The contract does not choose address wrap, bus, or timing behavior. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The private state contract exposes checked DP and CPL field accessors with explicit knownness, width, output-preserving rejection, and field-limited mutation behavior. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The private sequencer contract validates tagged direct DP/SP source arms, their canonical field domains, their value-owned operand/source relationship, and their exact CPL policy before reading architectural state. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The private direct DP/SP planners return explicit invalid-argument or unresolved-boundary statuses and an all-zero effect for rejected field or endpoint inputs while retaining no caller storage. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The indexed planner returns value-owned effects, rejects malformed fields and selected-AR0 aliasing with explicit statuses, rejects unselected unsigned boundary crossings as unresolved, and returns an all-zero effect for every non-OK result. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The sequencer validates the indexed source arm, canonical WORD16 and POST_ACCESS shape, and CMPT0/ARP0 policy before reading selected ARx then AR0; either dependency produces the generic unknown-source or stale-source status as applicable, and rejection preserves caller-owned state byte-for-byte while success commits at most the selected-AR write. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

Table 5-4 describes MOD12 as ARx plus a 16-bit long offset with ARx unchanged but does not explicitly classify that offset as signed or unsigned; it explicitly defines MOD13 as a signed 16-bit offset added before access, with the sum replacing ARx and supplying the operand address.

The long-offset indirect form carries a 16-bit long offset as part of the instruction and distinguishes addressing with and without an auxiliary-register update; this record does not assert signedness, instruction-fetch sequencing, repeat behavior, or timing.
Instruction class 9B defines a long-word read operand using long-offset indirect addressing; this record establishes operand access shape only and does not assert bus, cycle, or repeat behavior.
Instruction class 13B defines a long-word write operand using long-offset indirect addressing; this record establishes operand access shape only and does not assert bus, cycle, or repeat behavior.

The long-offset planner copies the raw 16-bit extension, sign-extends it explicitly, constructs canonical WORD16 or LONG32 effects with one selected-AR PRE_ACCESS update, rejects invalid fields and unsafe unsigned endpoints, and returns an all-zero effect for every non-OK result. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The sequencer validates the long-offset source arm and intrinsic MOD13 PRE_ACCESS shape before CMPT=0/ARP=0 and selected-AR state checks, preserves caller-owned state on rejection, and commits at most one selected-AR write without redoing offset arithmetic. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

Table 5-4 lists MOD4 *ARx-0B and MOD7 *ARx+0B: the old ARx value supplies the operand address and ARx is updated after access by reverse-carry subtraction or addition using AR0. This record makes no width-scaling or read/write-restriction claim beyond the table text.

The bit-reversed addressing discussion requires AR0=2^(N-1) for an FFT size 2^N, shows reverse-carry propagation from bit 15 (MSB) toward bit 0 (LSB), and provides the worked address sequence 0x60, 0x68, 0x64, 0x6c, 0x62, 0x6a, 0x66, 0x6e with its four-bit table.
Table 5-9 lists the *AR0-0B and *AR0+0B operand syntax as legal forms. This syntax record does not determine update ordering when the selected auxiliary register aliases AR0.

The project reverse-carry primitive has an explicit status and value contract, performs unsigned 16-bit bit-by-bit reverse propagation without signed shifts or implicit wrap selection, and exposes no usable candidate when propagation escapes the 16-bit domain. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The project reverse-carry planner exposes only WORD16 MOD4/MOD7 operands with CMPT=0, selected AR1-AR7, and a nonzero one-hot AR0 value; its validator rejects malformed non-WORD16 effects, invalid fields, non-one-hot AR0, and unresolved boundaries with deterministic statuses and an all-zero effect. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The sequencer reverse-carry transaction validates the tagged source arm and POST_ACCESS relation before ordered selected-AR then AR0 dependency reads, preserves complete state on rejection, and commits at most one selected-AR write without recomputing reverse-carry arithmetic. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

Section 3.3.4.8 defines BK as the 16-bit circular-buffer size register used by the ARAUs to specify the data-block size. This record does not claim circular arithmetic, memory mapping, reset, or timing behavior.
Table 3-3 maps the CPU memory-mapped BK circular-buffer size register to data-memory address 0x19. This is a mapping record only; it does not implement or claim common-core MMR routing.

The circular-addressing discussion defines BK as the circular-buffer size input and describes its relationship to the effective base, end, index, and step for future circular-addressing work. This record does not implement circular arithmetic or select boundary behavior.

Table 5-4 defines MOD8 as using the old ARx value for the operand followed by circular ARx minus one, and MOD10 as using the old ARx value followed by circular ARx plus one; this record covers WORD16 fixed one-word steps only and does not select boundary, LONG32, or timing behavior.

Section 5.5.3.4 defines circular addressing from BK size R: choose N as the smallest integer with 2^N greater than R, align the base to 2^N, derive the effective base and end plus the index from ARx and BK, and apply the step at that index; no adjustment occurs for 0 <= index+step < BK, subtract BK when index+step >= BK, and add BK when index+step < 0. BK=0 disables circular modification, and the first access AR must point inside the buffer. This record does not select unsupported operand forms or timing behavior.

The private BK state seam owns a copied 16-bit value with checked read/write accessors, explicit OK/UNKNOWN/INVALID_ARGUMENT status, output-preserving rejected reads, and knownness established only by a valid write. Reset leaves BK physically zero but architecturally unknown. This is a project contract, not TI reset or circular behavior evidence.

The private sequencer validation seam performs deterministic read-only address-effect validation in its documented dependency order, writes a zeroed commit description on every error, and leaves the sole architectural-state write to the apply boundary. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The circular address planner and intrinsic validator own checked CMPT=0 WORD16 MOD8/MOD10 effects with copied AR/BK source snapshots, strict argument and initial-buffer validation, canonical BK=0 NONE updates, and all-zero effects on rejected planner results. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The sequencer application contract validates circular effect shape and phase, reads CMPT/ARP before the selected AR and then BK, distinguishes unknown and stale dependencies, commits at most one selected-AR write for positive BK, and leaves canonical BK=0 NONE effects non-mutating. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.

locator.anchor: P2-W18: private program-PC bridge and CPU NOP transaction (active kickoff)

evidence.assertion: The P2-W18 project contract defines a standalone CPU transaction from the exact public program-word carrier through one 16-bit program-word fetch, decode, semantic dispatch, private 16-bit sequential-PC staging, and transactional retirement. An attempt begins immediately before the bus read, so bus faults and unknown decoded words count once; high carriers are passed unchanged to the bus and a known NOP above the private 16-bit domain fails bridge validation without truncation. The contract preserves state on failed stages, separates attempted from retired counters, bounds run calls by retirements or the first stop, and treats cumulative counter overflow as an explicit no-mutation stop. It makes no XPC, timing, interrupt, repeat, data-memory, device, observer, or emulator-integration claim. This is a project orchestration contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The P2-W19A project contract defines a pure, allocation-free extractor over a borrowed view of one or more 16-bit program words and a borrowed immutable field layout; it retains no pointers. Pieces identify a source word index, source LSB, width 1..16, and destination LSB 0..63; fields declare raw width 1..64, require in-word pieces, non-overlapping destination pieces that cover the declared value exactly, and non-overlapping source slices within each source word. Successful extraction publishes a caller-owned uint64_t raw value plus explicit width; invalid views, layouts, outputs, indexes, widths, overlap, or gaps leave output byte-for-byte unchanged. The contract makes no sign-extension, semantic, bus, CPU, state, PC, effect, timing, memory, interrupt, repeat, observer, diagnostic, file, environment, heap, mutable-global, or TI instruction-conformance claim.

locator.anchor: P2-W19B: transactional extension fetch and width-aware program PC (active kickoff)

evidence.assertion: The P2-W19B project contract freezes two standalone private seams before any multiword opcode integration. The instruction-fetch owner accepts a copied first program word and exact uint32_t first_program_word_address plus a bus descriptor and context borrowed for the call only, retains no pointer, and returns a fully initialized by-value result whose fixed program_words[2] bundle capacity is a helper limit rather than an ISA-wide maximum. Count zero and counts above two are rejected before I/O. Count one copies and publishes the supplied first word with zero callbacks. Count two admits high carriers, checks first_program_word_address+1 before exactly one callback at that exact carrier, and rejects UINT32_MAX overflow before I/O. Count one, invalid-bus, unsupported-count, and address-overflow results use TI_C54X_BUS_OK because no bus transaction was attempted; a missing count-two callback maps to a bus fault plus TI_C54X_BUS_NO_CALLBACK; callback failure maps to a bus fault while preserving its exact non-OK bus status. Every non-OK result zeroes the named bundle count and both words without retry. The helper owns no first-word fetch, counters, CPU/PC/state mutation, common 16-bit/XPC policy, timing, memory, observers, or diagnostics. Independently, the sequencer bridge and sequential-PC owners accept explicit widths 1..255, convert both operands to uint32_t before addition, reject count zero and sums above UINT16_MAX without wrap or narrowing, preserve one-word boundaries and transactional valid/stale/malformed effect behavior, reject public carriers above UINT16_MAX without XPC inference, and perform no bus I/O. This is a project contract, not TI conformance evidence.
The instruction summary lists RPT #K as a one-program-word form with K in the 0..255 range and RPT #lk as a two-program-word form with a 16-bit lk operand in the 0..65535 range.

The RPT operation encodes immediate #K as 0xEC00 with K in bits 7:0, encodes immediate #lk as first word 0xF070 followed by one 16-bit extension word, loads RC with the operand value, repeats the following instruction operand+1 times, changes no status bits, and is itself nonrepeatable. The examples establish #2 as three body executions and #0xffff as 65536 body executions.

The RPT description states that software cannot access RC while single-repeat execution is decrementing it. This establishes an active-repeat access restriction but does not identify the decrement phase or the architecturally visible value after the final body execution.

The MVDK and MVKD repeat descriptions make their automatic address increment conditional on the current RC value being nonzero and describe the total transfer count as the value in RC at instruction start plus one. This proves that a body-visible RC predicate matters to these repeated operations, but not when RC decrements or what value remains after completion.

READA execution pseudocode transfers the program word while RC is nonzero, increments PAR by one, and writes RC minus one to RC; when RC is zero it performs the terminal transfer without a PAR or RC update. Together with the RPT operand load and operand-plus-one cardinality, this establishes the externally observable RC decrement sequence and final zero for this documented RC-consuming repeated body; it does not claim internal decrement ordering, PC flow, or interrupt arbitration.

WRITA execution pseudocode transfers the data word while RC is nonzero, increments PAR by one, and writes RC minus one to RC; when RC is zero it performs the terminal transfer without a PAR or RC update. Together with the RPT operand load and operand-plus-one cardinality, this independently establishes the externally observable RC decrement sequence and final zero for this documented RC-consuming repeated body; it does not claim internal decrement ordering, PC flow, or interrupt arbitration.

FIRS execution pseudocode runs its repeated body while RC is nonzero and writes RC minus one to RC after each loop body, corroborating the documented RC decrement progression. This record does not claim the terminal extra-body rule, internal decrement ordering, PC flow, or interrupt arbitration.

The repeat restrictions define which instruction bodies and operand/addressing forms are nonrepeatable, including control-transfer and repeat-control instructions and long-offset or absolute single-data bodies. This record establishes eligibility as an explicit policy input and does not infer a broader eligible set.

After RPT is decoded, all interrupts including NMI are deferred until every execution of the repeated body completes, with the literal RS/reset exception remaining admissible. The repeat description does not settle the internal arbitration phase, RC decrement phase, or program-counter hold/reload details.
The pipeline interrupt discussion confirms that all executions of the repeated instruction complete before an interrupt executes, protecting the unsavable pipeline-parallel context.

The interrupt request and recognition descriptions state that a request sets its IFR flag regardless of immediate acknowledgement and that the corresponding flag is cleared when the interrupt is taken. This record does not select device-specific sources, vectors, or priority wiring.

The interrupt flag register description lists four clear events: RS reset, taking the corresponding interrupt trap, writing one to a corresponding IFR bit, and executing INTR with the appropriate interrupt number. A set bit denotes a pending interrupt; writing the current IFR value clears every currently set flag. This record does not select a bit assignment, request priority, or interrupt entry behavior.

locator.anchor: P2-W20E: pure single-repeat policy foundation (active kickoff)

evidence.assertion: The P2-W20E project contract defines three allocation-free, value-only policies under the dedicated repeat sequencer owner: checked uint16_t operand to uint32_t body-cardinality derivation, admission from the catalog's existing tri-state repeatability scalar without opcode inference, and a repeat-only request gate over an explicit remaining-body count plus maskable, NMI, or literal RS/reset class. Invalid inputs are explicit and transactional. These policies do not claim that a body executed, bind concrete opcode restrictions, sample or mutate IFR, progress RC, control PC, integrate CPU execution, or resolve predecode interrupt arbitration.

The P2-W48A project contract introduces typed checked RC access and one fixed-size, allocation-free repeat-progress reducer. A REPEAT_START effect transactionally loads RC and stores an exact uint32_t operand-plus-one remaining count. Each caller-reported successful body retirement validates the authoritative RC snapshot, decrements nonzero RC once, preserves terminal zero, and reaches COMPLETE only after the exact count. Unknown, stale, malformed, unsupported, and extra-completion paths preserve state. The seam owns no CPU dispatch, body PC flow, interrupt arbitration, bus work, timing, observer, diagnostic, environment, allocator, or mutable process state, and adds no branch to the current CPU path.

The P2-W48B project contract introduces typed checked IFR access and one fixed-size, caller-owned maskable pending-request reducer. Accepted requests validate a caller-selected one-bit IFR mask, set and preserve that bit while the existing repeat gate reports DEFER, and clear it on an explicit normal-take operation after the gate opens. Separate explicit IFR-write-one and INTR operations clear matching pending state; authoritative reset establishes known-zero IFR and an empty latch even from unknown IFR storage. Validation-dependent unknown, stale, malformed, and invalid-count paths preserve state. NMI representation, predecode arbitration, source and priority selection, CPU dispatch, PC, timing, allocation, I/O, observers, environment access, and mutable globals remain outside the seam, which adds no branch to the current CPU path.

locator.anchor: P2-W21A: private WORD16 bus-request contract (active kickoff)

evidence.assertion: The P2-W21A project contract defines a private, value-owned request for exactly one architectural 16-bit word. Separate read and write constructors carry an explicit program, data, or I/O space and an exact uint32_t word-address input; program requests preserve the full carrier while data and I/O requests reject values above UINT16_MAX before narrowing. Construction reports exactly OK, INVALID_SPACE, or INVALID_ADDRESS, validating space before its address domain. Read requests have a canonical zero write value, write requests copy the exact uint16_t value, and invalid results zero every named request field without making a bytewise-padding claim. The type itself fixes WORD16 width. The request owns no callback, read result, pointer, byte order, host storage, transaction phase, wait state, issue/completion state, timing, arbitration, CPU state, opcode effect, observer, or diagnostic behavior. This is a project structure contract, not TI conformance evidence.

The P2-W21B project contract defines private, pure by-value encode and decode results for one uint16_t word and exactly two uint8_t lanes under an explicit BIG or LITTLE byte-order argument. BIG maps 0x1234 to bytes 0x12,0x34 and LITTLE maps it to 0x34,0x12. Decode borrows exactly two readable bytes only until return, checks a null input before byte-order validity, and retains no pointer. Invalid results zero every named payload field without claiming padding-byte values. Implementations use value arithmetic rather than pointer casts, unions, packed objects, memcpy, or host-native order. The codec owns no global current order, program-image format, physical shared-memory lane policy, snapshot/wire format, callback, transaction, CPU state, or TI architectural endian claim.

The P2-W21C project contract defines a private, callback-free, allocation-free WORD16 reducer under src/bus/transaction/. Caller-declared canonical {0} storage carries lifecycle-only IDLE, ISSUE_READY, IN_FLIGHT, COMPLETION_READY, COMPLETE, and FAULT states plus a fresh nonzero caller-generated uint64_t transaction_id, copied valid W21A request, staged read word, and staged ti_c54x_bus_status. prepare copies a borrowed request only from IDLE; begin authorizes one issue and returns a copied request/id; repeated WAIT polling remains IN_FLIGHT without reissue; one READY or FAULT observation latches COMPLETION_READY; complete publishes canonical payload once; reset may clear only IDLE, COMPLETE, or FAULT and never cancels active work. Statuses are exactly OK, WAIT, FAULT, INVALID_ARGUMENT, INVALID_STATE, and STALE_TRANSACTION. Checked ARP and CMPT accessors reject null, unknown, and out-of-range inputs without mutating state or caller outputs, preserve unrelated field bits and knownness on valid writes, and expose only their documented field ranges.

Address-effect application validates state-policy tags explicitly, distinguishes UNKNOWN_MODE_STATE from MODE_STATE_VIOLATION, permits generic NONE without mode-state consultation, and rejects every policy failure transactionally without mutation.

The private address-effect application seam rejects null or malformed inputs in deterministic order, never interprets a non-OK planner payload, requires the requested phase and effective-address relation to match the intrinsic effect, distinguishes unknown and stale selected AR state, and leaves the complete state unchanged on every rejection; successful AR effects perform one checked write and NONE effects do not mutate state.

The private data-operand API exposes value-owned canonical WORD16 and LONG32 descriptors with no retained or embedded borrow; its validator temporarily borrows a read-only descriptor, accepts only the defined width and first/second-word relationships, mutates neither caller storage nor the descriptor, and leaves address wrap behavior unselected.

The private sequencer operand-application seam validates canonical operand shape before mode and auxiliary-register state, preserves the complete caller-owned state on every rejection, and applies accepted 32-bit effects transactionally without inferring wrap, bus, timing, or diagnostic behavior.

Checked DP and CPL accessors reject null, unknown, and out-of-range inputs without mutating state or caller outputs, preserve unrelated field bits and knownness on valid writes, and expose only their documented field ranges.
Tagged direct DP/SP source snapshots are value-owned and checked against their canonical field domains, recomputed WORD16 operand, and exact direct CPL policy before architectural state is read.
Direct-source application rejects malformed intrinsic payloads before phase, mode, or source-state checks and rejects non-OK planner results without interpreting their payloads.
Direct-source application distinguishes UNKNOWN_MODE_STATE for unreadable CPL from UNKNOWN_SOURCE for unreadable DP or SP and STALE_SOURCE for a mismatching known DP or SP snapshot.
Every rejected direct-source application preserves the complete caller-owned architectural state byte-for-byte, while accepted direct effects perform no address-register write.

For CMPT=0 MOD13 *+ARx(lk) WORD16 operands, interpret the copied raw lk word as a signed 16-bit offset, add it to selected ARx before access, use the resulting in-range data-word address, and replace ARx with that value.

For CMPT=0 MOD13 *+ARx(lk) LONG32 operands, apply the signed 16-bit offset before access to form the first in-range data-word address and represent the canonical MSW/LSW pair without scaling the offset by operand width.
Planner-produced CMPT=0 MOD13 effects carry the copied raw offset, a canonical WORD16 or LONG32 operand, and one PRE_ACCESS selected-AR update whose resulting address is used by the operand.

The signedness of the MOD12 long-offset carrier remains unresolved: the CPU description identifies a 16-bit long offset but does not explicitly classify it as signed or unsigned, so no MOD12 arithmetic is selected.

The long-offset planner copies its raw extension, performs explicit signed evaluation, validates MOD13 source and operand relations, rejects unsafe unsigned endpoints as unresolved, and returns an all-zero effect for every non-OK result.

Long-offset application validates intrinsic source, operand, and PRE_ACCESS shape before CMPT=0/ARP=0 and selected-AR state reads, reports unknown or stale selected-AR state deterministically, preserves complete state on rejection, and commits at most one selected-AR write.
Implement the common safe-domain 16-bit reverse-carry primitive: nonescaping propagation follows the documented bit direction over the represented word.
For a valid safe-domain WORD16 CMPT=0 MOD4 operand, the old selected AR supplies the operand address and a reverse-carry subtraction using AR0 supplies the post-access selected-AR update.
For a valid safe-domain WORD16 CMPT=0 MOD7 operand, the old selected AR supplies the operand address and a reverse-carry addition using AR0 supplies the post-access selected-AR update.

A valid reverse-carry WORD16 effect preserves the old selected-AR operand address, carries one POST_ACCESS selected-AR update, and retains the CMPT=0/ARP=0 state policy without claiming timing or bus behavior.
Final reverse-carry propagation, endpoint behavior, and 16-bit wrap semantics remain unresolved.
The ordering when selected AR0 aliases the reverse-carry index remains unresolved; legal *AR0±0B syntax does not establish whether the selected value or updated value is observed.
The applicability and update scaling of MOD4/MOD7 for LONG32 operands remain unresolved; no width scaling is inferred from the MOD1–MOD3-only access-width text.
The reverse-carry primitive has deterministic status and output rules, rejects propagation escape without silently wrapping, and remains free of signed-shift or implementation-defined arithmetic.

The reverse-carry planner owns validation and rejection precedence for MOD4/MOD7 WORD16 effects, requires selected AR1–AR7 and nonzero one-hot AR0, and returns an all-zero effect for every non-OK result.

The sequencer reverse-carry application contract validates source shape and ordered dependencies, preserves state byte-for-byte on rejection, and commits at most one selected-AR POST_ACCESS write without recomputing arithmetic.
Represent the documented common circular-buffer size register BK as a 16-bit architectural value without claiming reset behavior, circular arithmetic, or memory-mapped routing.

The private BK accessor contract keeps a copied 16-bit value with explicit OK/UNKNOWN/INVALID_ARGUMENT status, physically zeroes BK representation at reset while leaving its architectural value unknown, preserves rejected read outputs and state, and establishes knownness only through a valid write.
Expose BK at CPU data-memory MMR word address 0x0019 through a future bus/MMR route; state access remains owned by src/state.

CMPT=0 circular MOD8/MOD10 effects obtain a known 16-bit BK size through the state seam and apply the documented R/N/base/index/step algorithm; BK=0 carries the canonical NONE update and leaves the selected address register unmodified, while unsupported forms remain separate requirements.

For CMPT=0 WORD16 circular MOD8/MOD10 forms, admit any selected auxiliary register AR0-AR7, use the pre-access selected AR as the effective address, and produce a post-access circular decrement or increment by one data word respectively; behavior for an initial AR outside the documented buffer remains a separate unresolved requirement.

A valid CMPT=0 WORD16 MOD8/MOD10 effect carries the pre-access selected AR as its effective address and, for positive BK, one POST_ACCESS selected-AR circular update; BK=0 carries the canonical NONE update and leaves architectural state unmodified, while bus, memory, and timing behavior remain outside this slice.

The circular planner validates argument precedence, rejects an initial selected AR outside the documented buffer, copies AR/BK source snapshots, emits canonical BK=0 NONE updates, validates intrinsic effect shape, and returns an all-zero effect for every rejected planner result.

The circular sequencer application validates intrinsic effect shape and phase, orders CMPT/ARP then selected-AR then BK dependency reads, distinguishes unknown and stale sources, commits at most one selected-AR write for positive BK, and preserves the complete state on rejection or BK=0 NONE success.

The behavior for a circular operand whose initial selected AR is outside the buffer remains unresolved; the source requires the first access AR to point inside the buffer, but the project does not yet select rejection, normalization, or other handling.
The circular MOD8/MOD10 update scaling for LONG32 operands remains unresolved; the WORD16 fixed one-word evidence does not select whether access width changes the circular step.
The MOD9/MOD11 circular update semantics using AR0 as a step remain unresolved; no behavior is selected for source ordering, step snapshot, aliasing, or boundary handling.
The signed-offset circular behavior of MOD14 remains unresolved; no signed offset source, premodify ordering, or boundary combination is selected.
CMPT=1 and dual-indirect circular forms remain unresolved; no alternate register-file, operand sequencing, or circular update behavior is selected.

The private address-effect validation seam is read-only and deterministic, enforces the documented dependency and rejection order, zeroes its commit description on every error, and leaves the sole architectural-state write to the apply boundary.

The sole opcode catalog accepts canonical EXACT and MASKED 16-bit value/mask rows, preserves the existing exact NOP row and behavior, rejects invalid masks, widths, duplicate IDs or handlers, and rejects every pairwise overlap deterministically without a priority rule; no masked production instruction is registered.

The catalog subsystem's deterministic tools/isa/catalog/generate_opcode_lookup.py emits the checked-in immutable generated/isa/catalog/opcode_first_word.inc as a 65,536-entry uint16_t direct lookup; normal Make, CMake, and consumer builds remain compiler-only and Python-free, quality checks regenerate and reject stale output, and runtime performs no initialization, allocation, or mutable global-table update.

Within the valid common program-counter domain, the end-to-end CPU path fetches the evidenced one-word NOP, applies no NOP-owned status effect, and advances the common program counter by one program word as the sequential flow effect.
A zero instruction budget returns without invoking the program bus, decoding, semantic dispatch, or either execution counter, and without mutating CPU state.

Preserve the public 32-bit program-word carrier exactly through the program-bus callback, including high-carrier addresses used to classify unknown words; do not truncate the carrier or infer XPC/page semantics. A known decoded NOP at a carrier above 0xffff is rejected later with TI_C54X_STOP_UNSUPPORTED_PROGRAM_ADDRESS before any truncation and leaves committed state unchanged.

Each instruction attempt requests exactly one 16-bit program word through the caller-owned program bus at the exact public 32-bit carrier before decode, without fetching an extension word in this slice; private 16-bit bridge validation occurs only after a known instruction is decoded.

An instruction attempt begins immediately before the program-bus read. A program-bus fetch failure therefore stops execution after exactly one attempted instruction but before decode, semantic dispatch, retirement, or PC mutation, and is not retried in the same instruction-budget step.

An unknown fetched word stops execution after the successful fetch but before semantic dispatch, leaves the private and public PC unchanged, and contributes exactly one attempted instruction but no retirement.

A known NOP dispatches through the generated catalog and semantic function-pointer seam; its handler contributes no opcode-owned architectural, status, bus, memory, device, or observer mutation, leaving PC staging to the sequencer.

The private program-PC bridge accepts the public 32-bit carrier and explicit program-word count, validates the carrier before deriving the common 16-bit PC, stages a checked sequential successor without consulting XPC, and exposes an explicit status plus value-owned public/common before/after words for transactional CPU orchestration.

The private program-PC bridge accepts 0xfffe to 0xffff, while a one-word instruction staged at 0xffff maps to TI_C54X_STOP_UNRESOLVED_PROGRAM_BOUNDARY before retirement and leaves the committed PC unchanged.

The private bridge commits only a valid staged effect whose frozen public source matches the live carrier; invalid or stale effects and unsupported or unresolved plans leave the caller-owned carrier and caller-owned effect output unchanged.

The CPU commits a staged sequential PC only after semantic dispatch and bridge validation succeed; rejected fetch, decode, semantic, carrier, or boundary stages preserve the committed PC and do not retire.

The attempted counter increments exactly once immediately before each program-bus read, so bus failures and unknown decoded words count as one attempted instruction; a zero budget and cumulative-counter preflight failure count zero. The retired counter increments exactly once only after semantic effects and PC commit both succeed; failed or unresolved steps do not retire.
An instruction-budget run returns after exactly N successful retirements or at the first explicit stop, whichever comes first, and never overshoots the requested retirement count.

Cumulative attempted and retired counter overflow is detected before mutation and produces TI_C54X_STOP_COUNTER_OVERFLOW with no fetch or counter mutation; counters must not silently wrap, and the overflow policy remains a planned executable contract until tested.

Implement a pure, allocation-free operand-field extractor over a borrowed caller-owned view of one or more 16-bit program words and a borrowed immutable layout. A field contains one or more pieces with a source word index, source LSB, width 1..16, and destination/value LSB 0..63, and declares raw width 1..64. Pieces must stay within source words and the declared destination width; destination pieces must not overlap and must cover the declared value exactly; source slices must not overlap within a source word. Successful extraction assembles a caller-owned uint64_t raw value plus explicit width for first-word, extension-word, split/non-contiguous, and 64-bit mechanics. Null or invalid views/layouts/outputs, out-of-range indexes, invalid widths, overlap, or gaps must leave output byte-for-byte unchanged. The extractor performs no sign extension or semantic interpretation and owns no bus, CPU, state, PC/effect, timing, memory, interrupt/repeat, observer, diagnostic, file, environment, heap, or mutable-global behavior.

The private instruction-fetch helper collects only extension words after a first word has already been fetched and decoded. It accepts a copied first word and exact uint32_t first_program_word_address plus a bus descriptor and context borrowed for the call only, retains no pointer, and returns an allocation-free, fully initialized by-value result whose bundle has helper capacity exactly two program words rather than an ISA-wide maximum. Count zero and counts above two are rejected before I/O. Count one copies and publishes the supplied first word with zero callbacks. Count two checks first_program_word_address+1 before exactly one callback at that exact carrier, admits high carriers without truncation, and rejects UINT32_MAX overflow before I/O. Count one, invalid-bus, unsupported-count, and address-overflow results use TI_C54X_BUS_OK because no bus transaction was attempted; a missing count-two callback maps to a bus fault with TI_C54X_BUS_NO_CALLBACK; callback failure maps to a bus fault while preserving its exact non-OK bus status. Every non-OK result zeroes the named bundle program_word_count and both words without retry, including when a callback scribbles before failing. The helper owns no first-word fetch, attempts, retirements, CPU/PC/state mutation, common 16-bit/XPC policy, timing, memory effects, observers, or diagnostics.

The private sequential-PC and public program-PC bridge seams accept explicit program_word_count values from 1 through 255, convert both operands to uint32_t before checked addition for 16-bit-int hosts, reject count zero and any sum above UINT16_MAX without wrapping or narrowing before validation, and preserve transactional valid/stale/malformed effect behavior. Count one preserves the admitted 0xfffe-to-0xffff transition and unresolved one-word source at 0xffff; count two admits 0xfffd-to-0xffff and rejects 0xfffe as unresolved. The public bridge rejects carriers above UINT16_MAX without XPC inference and delegates admitted width arithmetic; no bus I/O is performed.

Define one copied, value-owned instruction-word bundle under the decode owner and use it as the complete-instruction handoff among CPU fetch, decode, and semantic dispatch. The current fixed capacity remains an explicit helper limit rather than an ISA-wide maximum; no pointer is retained, failures publish no partial bundle, and CPU fetch owns population rather than the value type or interpretation.

Require every sole-inventory opcode row to name a catalog-owned scalar operand-layout token and tri-state repeatability classification, carry both through immutable metadata and the copied decoded-instruction value, and validate them outside opcode semantics. UNKNOWN layout tokens are never valid for a production row; UNRESOLVED repeatability is explicit and must never imply eligibility.

Resolve every production catalog row's scalar operand-layout identity through immutable decode-owned static descriptors, validate instruction width and binding outside opcode semantics, and produce copied operands through the shared field extractor so handlers never hand-mask encoded words. Layout sets support zero, one, or multiple fields; the catalog remains the sole inventory and runtime metadata remains immutable and initialization-free.

Given a copied operand-field value already extracted from either inert immediate-RPT layout, build one discriminated value-owned REPEAT_START effect that carries the exact unsigned 16-bit operand without retaining caller storage. Invalid inputs leave output byte-for-byte unchanged. The effect is not a claim of production decode, dispatch, RC mutation, repeat cardinality, sequencing, interrupt behavior, or CPU consumption.

Derive a copied uint32_t body-execution cardinality equal to a copied uint16_t repeat operand plus one, including 65536 for operand 0xffff, without narrow arithmetic or mutation. Invalid arguments leave caller-owned output unchanged. This pure policy does not claim that any instruction body executed or define RC or PC behavior.

Map the existing catalog-owned repeatability scalar to an explicit repeat-body admission decision: ELIGIBLE admits, INELIGIBLE rejects, and UNRESOLVED remains non-admitting and distinct. Invalid arguments or forged enum values leave caller-owned output unchanged; no opcode identity, width, operand, or addressing form is inferred.

Given a caller-supplied body-execution count remaining in the range zero through 65536 and an explicit maskable, NMI, or literal RS/reset request class, report only the repeat gate's decision: an inactive gate blocks nothing, an active gate defers maskable and NMI requests, and literal RS/reset is never blocked. Invalid inputs leave caller-owned output unchanged. The policy owns no request sampling, IFR state, acknowledgement, priority, vector, or device wiring.

Provide typed checked access to the private 16-bit RC storage and its dedicated knownness bit. Reads publish only a known value and otherwise preserve caller output; writes accept every uint16_t value, mutate only RC plus its knownness bit, retain no pointer, and perform no sequencing, allocation, I/O, observation, diagnostics, or environment access.

Consume a value-owned REPEAT_START effect into a fixed-size caller-owned progress value and authoritative architectural RC state. Start widens before deriving operand-plus-one remaining bodies; a reported successful body retirement validates active phase, count bounds, RC knownness, and the exact remaining-minus-one RC invariant before decrementing nonzero RC once or preserving terminal zero. Completion occurs only when the remaining count reaches zero. Null, unsupported, active-restart, forged, stale, unknown, and extra-completion paths preserve both state and progress. The reducer is allocation-free and owns no CPU, PC, interrupt, bus, timing, observer, diagnostic, environment, or mutable-global behavior.

Provide typed checked access to private 16-bit IFR storage and its dedicated knownness bit. Reads publish only a known value and otherwise preserve caller output; full writes accept every uint16_t value and establish knownness; one-bit set and clear operations accept exactly one nonzero bit, preserve unrelated flags and every other architectural field, and reject invalid or unknown state transactionally. The accessor retains no pointer and owns no request sequencing, allocation, I/O, observation, diagnostics, environment access, or mutable global state.

Provide one fixed-size, caller-owned lifecycle for a maskable request identified by exactly one caller-selected IFR bit. Receipt sets the bit before the existing repeat gate reports deferred or eligible; an active gate prevents take and preserves both bit and latch, while an explicit take after the gate opens clears both. Separate IFR-write-one and INTR clear operations remove matching pending state; authoritative reset establishes known-zero IFR and an empty latch. Null, validation-dependent unknown, stale, forged, duplicate, invalid-mask, and invalid-count paths preserve caller state. The reducer owns no NMI mapping, source or priority selection, predecode arbitration, CPU dispatch, PC, timing, allocation, I/O, observers, environment access, or mutable globals and adds no current CPU hot-path branch.

Construct and validate a private value-owned request for exactly one architectural 16-bit word. Separate read and write construction names program, data, or I/O space and consumes an exact uint32_t word-address input without I/O: program requests preserve the full carrier, while data and I/O reject addresses above UINT16_MAX before narrowing. Construction reports exactly OK, INVALID_SPACE, or INVALID_ADDRESS and validates space before its address domain. Read requests carry a canonical zero write value; write requests copy the exact uint16_t value. Invalid construction zeroes every named request field without requiring padding bytes to have a value. The request retains no pointer and owns no callback, result payload, byte order, host memory, transaction phase, wait/lifecycle state, arbitration, CPU state, opcode effect, timing, observation, or diagnostics.

Encode one copied uint16_t word into exactly two value-owned uint8_t lanes and decode two borrowed lanes into one copied uint16_t under an explicit BIG or LITTLE byte order. BIG maps 0x1234 to 0x12,0x34 and LITTLE to 0x34,0x12; both orders round-trip the full uint16_t domain. Decode rejects null input before checking a forged order and retains no pointer. Invalid results zero every named payload field. The implementation uses shifts, masks, and explicit scalar conversion only, with no aliasing cast, union, packed object, memcpy, host-order inference, global order, image/shared-memory/snapshot policy, callback, transaction, CPU state, timing, or diagnostics.

Decode RPT #K as one program word matching value 0xEC00 and mask 0xFF00 with the unsigned operand in bits 7:0, and decode RPT #lk as exact first word 0xF070 followed by one complete unsigned 16-bit extension-word operand.
For either immediate RPT form, carry the exact decoded operand as the value loaded into RC and produce no status-bit effect; the operation itself is nonrepeatable.
Execute the instruction following immediate RPT exactly operand+1 times, including one execution for operand zero and 65536 executions for operand 0xffff, without counter wrap.
After RPT decode and until every repeated-body execution completes, defer maskable requests and NMI while still admitting literal RS/reset; no request may be serviced between body executions.

After an accepted maskable request arrives while the post-decode single-repeat gate is active, set and preserve its caller-selected IFR bit while acknowledgement is deferred; when that deferred request is explicitly reported taken through normal service, clear that bit. Reset, explicit IFR writes, INTR-triggered clearing, NMI representation, bit assignment, priority selection, and requests already pending before RPT decode remain outside this requirement.

Reject a single-repeat body when its instruction or operand/addressing form is classified nonrepeatable by the documented restrictions, including repeat-control and control-transfer bodies and long-offset or absolute single-data forms.
Resolve the exact RC decrement phase during single-repeat execution and the architecturally visible final RC value before integrating repeat retirement into the CPU.

For a documented RC-consuming single-repeat body, RC starts at the RPT operand K; each nonterminal body observes RC greater than zero and decrements it exactly once after the body operation, while the terminal body observes RC equal to zero and leaves RC at zero. This requirement claims only externally observable RC progression and final value; internal decrement ordering, repeated-body PC microflow, and interrupt arbitration remain outside its scope.
Resolve how the repeated-body program counter is held or reloaded and the exact final program counter after single-repeat completion before CPU integration.
Resolve whether and at which phase an already-pending request may be taken before the RPT post-decode gate becomes active.

Implement a pure callback-free allocation-free WORD16 transaction reducer with caller-declared canonical {0} storage and lifecycle-only IDLE, ISSUE_READY, IN_FLIGHT, COMPLETION_READY, COMPLETE, and FAULT states. prepare copies a valid W21A request and fresh nonzero caller-generated transaction_id only from IDLE; begin authorizes exactly one issue and returns a copied request/id; repeated WAIT polling remains IN_FLIGHT; one READY or FAULT observation latches COMPLETION_READY; complete publishes one canonical result and enters COMPLETE or FAULT; reset permits only IDLE, COMPLETE, or FAULT and never cancels active work. Stale nonmatching IDs are rejected, the caller must maintain one authoritative storage instance without copying it by value while active, and exactly-once is a protocol claim only under caller ownership and unique-ID preconditions.

The WORD16 transaction reducer validates null pointers first, canonical transaction state and legal lifecycle next, zero IDs as invalid arguments, nonmatching nonzero IDs as STALE_TRANSACTION, and observation tag/payload shape last. Statuses are exactly OK, WAIT, FAULT, INVALID_ARGUMENT, INVALID_STATE, and STALE_TRANSACTION; FAULT preserves only known non-OK ti_c54x_bus_status values, WAIT and READY carry TI_C54X_BUS_OK, WAIT and FAULT read payloads are zero, READY writes carry a zero read payload, failed result payloads are zero, and rejected transitions preserve every named field without making a C-padding claim.

The W31B adapter proof must demonstrate actual endpoint issue and completion counts, commit-at-READY physical visibility across WAIT suspension, and exactly-once read/write effects when consuming the public copied DATA WORD16 protocol. The W21C reducer does not fabricate those effects; deterministic arbitration, device profiles, and posted writes remain separate later proofs.
Decode the one-word LD #k9,DP form with value 0xEA00 and mask 0xFE00, extracting an unsigned 9-bit field and classifying it as single-repeat INELIGIBLE.
Decode the one-word LD #k5,ASM form with value 0xED00 and mask 0xFFE0, extracting a raw 5-bit field representing -16..15; repeatability remains unresolved and is not inferred.
Decode the one-word LD #k3,ARP form with value 0xF4A0 and mask 0xFFF8, extracting a 3-bit field and classifying it as single-repeat INELIGIBLE.
Execute the three evidenced one-word immediate LD status-field forms by producing value-owned DP, ASM, and ARP target effects from their raw fields, with no other status-bit side effects.

Provide the private status-register subownership required by the three P2-W22 LD forms: expose checked DP, ASM, and ARP field access and preserve unrelated status bits and knownness without introducing a raw snapshot or persistence ABI.

Apply one validated value-owned DP, ASM, or ARP effect transactionally, preserving unrelated status fields and leaving state unchanged on rejection. This private effect seam exists only for the P2-W22 forms and does not claim timing, memory, interrupt, or device behavior.

The CPU-owned vertical-slice seam observes a validated P2-W22 status-field effect and commits exactly one DP, ASM, or ARP update atomically at instruction retirement. ti_c54x_state may grow observation fields before stability; these fields do not define a raw snapshot or persistence ABI and no stable persistence guarantee is made. This is a project transaction contract, not a timing, memory, interrupt, or device claim.

Decode MAX and MIN as four exact one-word encodings derived from the TI opcode diagrams: MAX 0xF486/0xFEFF and MIN 0xF487/0xFEFF, with D=0 selecting A and D=1 selecting B. Reject mask near-misses and preserve the canonical decoded instruction transactionally.

Produce a value-owned MAX/MIN compare-select effect over signed full 40-bit A/B values, including guard bits: MAX selects A on A>=B and MIN selects A on A<=B, ties included; the selected value targets D, C is 0 for A and 1 for B, and no other architectural field is changed.

Validate and apply MAX/MIN through the generic value-owned ACCUMULATOR_WRITE effect only at retirement. The handler receives a copied, read-only A/B input snapshot, owns compare/select correctness, and emits the explicit C WRITE action; the effect carries no source snapshots. The sequencer validates destination, a canonical 40-bit two's-complement selected value, the C action, and one-bit C before atomically committing the candidate accumulator plus C state; structurally invalid or rejected effects preserve both accumulators and the complete status state.

Own canonical full-40-bit A/B accumulator storage with checked internal read/write, explicit knownness, unknown-after-common-reset behavior, rejection nonmutation, and cross-accumulator isolation. This private state seam does not introduce a premature public set-state or bootstrap API.

Before dispatch, obtain a checked immutable A/B input snapshot through the accumulator state owner. If either source is unknown, stop with INVALID_STATE without retirement or mutation; otherwise execute each MAX/MIN destination encoding through the public CPU path with one attempt and one retirement, sequential PC +1, destination-only accumulator mutation, exact C result, and unknown-word stop. CPU tests may seed through the state owner's checked internal API; no public set-state/bootstrap API is implied, and no timing or memory behavior is claimed.

MAX and MIN repeatability is unresolved: TI Table 2-28 does not list them, but its preamble does not state that every unlisted instruction is repeatable. Do not classify either form as ELIGIBLE until positive evidence or an explicit project policy resolves this boundary.

Rename the select-named accumulator effect to generic ACCUMULATOR_WRITE and validate a value-owned destination, canonical full-40-bit value, and explicit C action. PRESERVE requires c_value=0; WRITE requires c_value=0 or 1; unknown actions, invalid destinations, and noncanonical payloads reject without mutating either accumulator, C, or unrelated status state. The transaction applies exactly once and atomically.

Decode CMPL as four exact one-word forms from value 0xF493 and mask 0xFCFF, with S at bit 9 selecting source A/B and D at bit 8 selecting destination A/B. A generic ACCUMULATOR_SOURCE_DESTINATION layout exposes source as operand 0 and destination as operand 1. Exhaustive 65,536-word lookup coverage must classify exactly those four forms, reject every fixed-bit near-miss, and preserve unrelated catalog rows.

Produce a pure CMPL effect that writes the full 40-bit one's complement of the selected source accumulator to the selected destination. The effect uses C PRESERVE, leaves c_value at canonical zero, and changes no status field or non-destination accumulator.

Route CMPL through the generic ACCUMULATORS input-resource mask and ACCUMULATOR_WRITE effect path. Retire each one-word form atomically with one attempt and one sequential PC increment, preserving C and unrelated state; no opcode-identity branch or new CPU file growth is permitted.

CMPL repeatability is unresolved: Table 2-28 does not list CMPL, but its preamble does not positively authorize every unlisted form. Do not classify CMPL as repeat-eligible until positive evidence or explicit project policy resolves the boundary.

Own one generic transactional input collector for resource masks. STATUS_C is a first-class resource beside ACCUMULATORS; the copied input snapshot carries a typed status_c value and status_c_known flag. The collector rejects unknown resource bits and invalid requested backing pointers, reads only requested resources, reads C once when requested, returns canonical zero/false for unrequested values, preserves A/B unknownness as data, and leaves output unchanged on rejection. It has no globals, environment reads, allocation, logging, or diagnostics, and the CPU uses one generic call without opcode identity branching.

Register ROL as value 0xF491/mask 0xFEFF and ROR as value 0xF490/mask 0xFEFF. Each form consumes exactly one program word and S at bit 8 selects the in-place accumulator A or B, producing exactly four populated encodings without claiming that encoded words are distinct instructions.

Decode ROL/ROR through a generic ACCUMULATOR_SOURCE layout extracting S from word 0 bit 8. Exhaustive 65,536-word lookup coverage must classify exactly 0xF491, 0xF591, 0xF490, and 0xF590, reject canonical fixed-bit and layout near-misses, and preserve all unrelated catalog rows.

Produce pure ROL/ROR effects over the selected accumulator's low 32 bits and pre-C: ROL inserts pre-C at bit 0 and writes old bit 31 to C; ROR inserts pre-C at bit 31 and writes old bit 0 to C. Clear guard bits 39:32, preserve the non-selected accumulator and every other status field, and emit the existing generic accumulator-write plus C-write effect.

Route ROL/ROR through ACCUMULATORS|STATUS_C input resources and the existing generic effect transaction. Unknown selected source or unknown C blocks retirement while unknown unselected accumulator data is allowed; admitted forms preserve unrelated status, retire exactly once with one attempt and PC+1, and reject at PC 0xffff without mutation. No opcode-specific CPU branch or CPU growth is permitted.

ROL and ROR repeatability is unresolved: Table 2-28 does not list either form, but its preamble does not positively authorize every unlisted form. Do not classify ROL or ROR as repeat-eligible until positive evidence or explicit project policy resolves the boundary.

Register SFTL_ACC/sftl_acc as value 0xF0E0 with mask 0xFCE0. The form consumes one program word, admits signed shifts -16..15, and produces exactly 128 source/destination/shift encodings without treating populated first-word entries as distinct instruction count.

Decode SFTL through TI_C54X_OPERAND_LAYOUT_ACCUMULATOR_SOURCE_DESTINATION_SHIFT5: source bit 9 is operand 0, destination bit 8 is operand 1, and raw shift bits 4:0 are operand 2.
